blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (GET /invoices/:id returns any organization's invoice) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Insecure direct object reference (CWE-639 / CWE-862). Any signed-in user of organization 7 who sends `GET /invoices/42` gets invoice 42 even when it belongs to another organization, and can enumerate every customer's invoices by walking the ids. Scope the lookup to the caller like the list does — `WHERE id = $1 AND org_id = $2` with `[id, currentUser(req).orgId]` — and keep answering 404 when no row matches, so foreign ids are indistinguishable from missing ones. Add a test asserting the query is scoped by `org_id`.
findings.title: GET /invoices/:id returns any organization's invoice

findings.recommendation: Information exposure through an error message (CWE-209). `express.json()` runs before `requireUser`, so an unauthenticated client that POSTs a malformed JSON body to any path gets the body-parser error forwarded here and receives the full stack trace (server file paths, node_modules layout and versions); any other error reaching the handler (database errors included) leaks its message the same way. Keep logging the error server-side, but answer a generic body such as `{ "error": "internal error" }` (and the error's own status, e.g. 400 for `err.status`/`err.expose` errors, instead of a blanket 500).
findings.title: Error handler returns the error message and stack trace to any client

findings.recommendation: The boundary check accepts any integer-valued number, so a signed-in user who sends `GET /invoices/100000000000000000000` (or `/invoices/1e20`) passes validation and the query fails in PostgreSQL with "out of range for type integer". With express 4.19.2 (package.json) a rejected promise in an async handler is not forwarded to the error handler: the request hangs and the rejection is unhandled, which terminates the process under Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` — one request takes the API down for everyone. Validate with an allow-list (`/^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$/` and an upper bound matching the column type) and wrap the async handlers so rejections reach `next(err)`.
findings.title: Invoice id is not range-checked and a database error escapes the async handler
